title: NOT EVERY RULE IS THE SAME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Anyone who sells a house in a walled city retains the right of redemption
a full year after its sale. During that time the seller may redeem it. If
it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled
city shall belong permanently to the buyer and the buyer's descendants. It
is not to be returned in the Jubilee'" - Lev 25:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the law makes a careful distinction. A house inside a walled city
followed different rules from farmland. It could be redeemed for one year,
but after that the sale became permanent and was not reversed at Jubilee.

Why the difference? Farmland was tied to a family's God-given inheritance
and their ability to feed themselves. A city house was more like ordinary
property. God's law was not a rigid, one-size-fits-all system; it made wise
distinctions between different kinds of situations.

Dear friend, there is wisdom to learn here. God is not simplistic, and He
does not want us to be either. Real love and real justice require the
ability to tell one situation from another. The same action can be
generous in one setting and foolish in another.

Paul prayed that the Philippians' love would abound more and more in
knowledge and depth of insight, so that they could discern what is best
(Phil 1:9-10). Mature faith is not about applying the same response to
everything; it is about discernment.

We sometimes want a simple formula for every decision. God more often calls
us to wisdom — to weigh each situation prayerfully and act accordingly.

Ask God for discernment today, not just rules. He gives wisdom generously
to those who ask (Jas 1:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I looking for simple formulas where God calls for discernment?
2. Where do I need wisdom to tell one situation from another?
3. How can I grow in depth of insight this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, give me not just rules but wisdom. Help me discern what is best in
each situation and act with love and insight. Amen.
